LESSON: INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS IN AFRICAN SOCIETIES CONSERVATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.2: Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does indigenous knowledge influence the modern society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity
2. explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life
3. use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS IN AFRICAN SOCIETIES CONSERVATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS IN AFRICAN SOCIETIES CONSERVATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity

What this means
In this part you learn to identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life

What this means
In this part you learn to explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life

What this means
In this part you learn to use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation. (skill: explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity.
3. Practise this skill: explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life.
4. Practise this skill: use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision-making in life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does indigenous knowledge influence the modern society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies Conservation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self- identity.
5. Be able to: explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for the sustainability of life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
